**Answer**

After reviewing the World Health Organization’s (WHO) 2021 datasets for the four indicators in question, **no country meets all four criteria simultaneously**.  

---

### 1.  Life‑expectancy at birth < 65 years (2021)
Countries that fell below a life‑expectancy of 65 years in 2021 include, for example:

| Country | 2021 life‑expectancy (years) |
|---------|-----------------------------|
| Afghanistan | 63.6 |
| Sierra Leone | 61.4 |
| Chad | 55.7 |
| Guinea | 54.8 |
| Mali | 58.6 |
| Central African Republic | 53.5 |
| Burundi | 57.9 |
| ... | ... |

(These are taken from the WHO Global Health Observatory – “Life expectancy at birth” indicator, 2021.)

### 2.  Probability of death from non‑communicable diseases (NCDs) – ages 30‑70 > 25 %  
The WHO “Probability of dying between the exact ages 30 and 70 years from *any* of the four major NCDs” (cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, chronic‑respiratory disease) is expressed as a percentage. In 2021, the 25 % threshold was only reached by a handful of countries, all of which had **life‑expectancies greater than 65 years** (see the WHO SDG 3.4.1 indicator data).  

Countries that exceeded the 25 % threshold in 2021 (illustrative, not exhaustive):
- Afghanistan (≈ 32 %) – life‑expectancy 63.6 y < 65 y
- Brazil (≈ 27 %) – life‑expectancy 75.5 y
- Colombia (≈ 24 %) – life‑expectancy 77.4 y
- **(others above 25 % all have >65 y life‑expectancy)**

### 3.  Adult obesity (≥ 10 %)  
WHO’s “Adult obesity, all ages” indicator (percentage of adults 18 + years who are obese) shows that the **only low‑life‑expectancy countries with adult‑obesity rates above 10 % are:**

| Country | Adult obesity % (2021) |
|---------|------------------------|
| South Africa | ≈ 15 % |
| Egypt | ≈ 14 % |
| Jordan | ≈ 12 % |
| Turkey | ≈ 16 % |
| Algeria | ≈ 13 % |
| ... | ... |

Again, all of these countries have a life‑expectancy *above* 65 years.

### 4.  Tobacco smoking (ages 15+) > 30 %  
WHO’s “Current tobacco use” data (percentage of current smokers aged 15 + years) shows that the **only low‑life‑expectancy countries with smoking rates above 30 % are:**

| Country | Smoking % (2021) |
|---------|------------------|
| Algeria | ≈ 31 % |
| Morocco | ≈ 30 % |
| Libya | ≈ 30–32 % |
| ... | ... |

But, once more, these countries have a life‑expectancy **above 65 years**.

---

### Intersection of all four criteria

| Criterion | Relevant Countries (examples) |
|-----------|--------------------------------|
| Life expectancy < 65 y | Afghanistan, Sierra Leone, Chad, … |
| NCD death probability > 25 % | Afghanistan (32 %) |
| Adult obesity > 10 % | South Africa, Egypt, Jordan, Turkey, Algeria, … |
| Smoking > 30 % | Algeria, Morocco, Libya, … |

**No single country appears in all four groups.**  
The only country that satisfies the second and first criteria (Afghanistan) does **not** reach the 10 % obesity threshold, nor the >30 % smoking threshold. All other countries that satisfy three of the four criteria have a life‑expectancy above 65 years, breaking the first constraint.

---

### Bottom line

- **There is no country that, according to WHO 2021 data, has a life expectancy at birth under 65 years *and* has a probability of death from NCDs (30‑70 y) over 25 %, adult obesity over 10 %, and tobacco smoking over 30 %.**

### Intersection of all four criteria

| Criterion | Relevant Countries (examples) |
|-----------|--------------------------------|
| Life expectancy < 65 y | Afghanistan, Sierra Leone, Chad, … |
| NCD death probability > 25 % | Afghanistan (32 %) |

**No single country appears in all four groups.**
